articles.title: Anthropic taps nonprofits METR and SecureBio to help assess risks and safety practices
articles.preview: Anthropic is partnering with independent evaluators to assess its AI safety practices. This move follows a proposal to slow down AI model development and includes collaborations with organizations like METR and SecureBio.

summary.t: Anthropic announced a plan to integrate third-party evaluators into its operations. This initiative was spurred by CEO Dario Amodei's proposal to slow down AI model development. The company is working with organizations like METR and SecureBio to verify adherence to safety practices.

Anthropic is establishing a tiered system for evaluators, offering varying levels of access and involvement. The first tier allows for narrowly scoped risk investigations, while the second tier enables report publication without company approval. The third tier provides employee-like access, as exemplified by METR’s onboarding of six employees.
METR, specializing in Model Evaluation and Threat Research, is a third-tier evaluator with six employees.

articles.title: SpaceX AI policy leader grilled by NYC Council on Grok safety, sexualized images
articles.preview: SpaceX’s AI policy leader, Gabriela Castillo Madrid, faced intense scrutiny from the New York City Council regarding the safety and potential misuse of its AI model, Grok. The council’s investigation centered around concerns about sexually explicit images generated by the AI and the company’s safeguards.

summary.t: NYC Council Speaker Julie Menin and other council members raised serious concerns about the safety of Grok, specifically after Menin herself encountered a sexually explicit image of her generated by the AI. Council Member Carmen De La Rosa criticized the company’s claims of safeguards, stating that the system enabled the easy sexualization of images without consent. The council’s investigation aims to guide new regulations regarding advanced AI models.

Former SpaceX and X employee, Devin Kim, testified before the council, detailing his concerns about AI safety that were allegedly dismissed by his manager. Kim, now with the Center for AI Safety, explained his role in building and evaluating Grok’s systems. He revealed that the company previously considered ‘tasteful nudity’ acceptable and that only three employees focused on AI safety, leading to significant departures.

Councilmember Mercedes Narcisse questioned SpaceX about the promotion of uploading X-rays to Grok, raising concerns about HIPAA protections and the potential for dangerous health advice. Castillo Madrid responded that Grok is not intended as a medical tool, and users control whether their conversations are used for training. The council criticized her responses for their vagueness.
SpaceX’s merger with xAI and subsequent acquisition of Cursor has placed Grok in use by federal agencies like the Pentagon.

articles.title: OpenAI Saudi national bugging case shows threat to U.S. leadership in AI: DNI Clayton
articles.preview: The recent case involving a Saudi national spying on OpenAI highlights a growing threat to U.S. AI leadership.

summary.t: A Saudi national, Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested for allegedly installing a recording device in an OpenAI executive conference room. The charge involves the interception of oral communications, not espionage. Alfozan had booked a one-way ticket to Saudi Arabia prior to his arrest.
Director Clayton stated that commercial and state-sponsored espionage are realities. Both the U.S. government and private companies need to be cautious of these threats.

articles.title: KI: Bundesregierung plant Kooperation mit US-Chiphersteller Nvidia
articles.preview: Die Bundesregierung plant eine Kooperation mit dem US-Chiphersteller Nvidia. Ziel ist es, Deutschland im Bereich Künstliche Intelligenz zu stärken und Investitionen anzuziehen.

summary.t: Die Bundesregierung hat eine Kooperation mit Nvidia, einem führenden Hersteller von Chips für Rechenzentren, vereinbart. Diese Zusammenarbeit soll die Entwicklung und Anwendung von Künstlicher Intelligenz in der Industrie vorantreiben.
Die Regierung erwartet am kommenden Montag und Dienstag rund 200 Unternehmen auf der Konferenz "Invest in Germany" in Berlin. Kanzler Merz plant bereits einen Treffen mit Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Anthropic öffnet sich für externe Prüfer
Hohe Millioneninvestition: Bundesregierung erwägt KI-Partnerschaft mit Nvidia
articles.preview: Die Bundesregierung plant eine strategische Partnerschaft mit dem Technologiekonzern Nvidia. Ziel ist es, die Entwicklung und den Einsatz von Künstlicher Intelligenz in Deutschland voranzutreiben.

summary.t: Die Bundesregierung beabsichtigt, einen dreistelligen Millionenbetrag in ein Projekt zu investieren, das sich auf die Entwicklung von KI konzentriert. Diese Finanzierung soll insbesondere die Nutzung von Rechenkapazitäten einer KI-Cloud der Deutschen Telekom unterstützen. Die Partnerschaft soll die Grundlage für den Einsatz von physischer KI schaffen, beispielsweise für das Training von Robotern und autonomen Fahrzeugen.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urges U.S.-China dialogue on 'potentially dangerous' AI
articles.preview: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is advocating for U.S.-China collaboration on AI safety. He believes open dialogue is crucial to mitigating potential risks associated with the rapidly developing technology.

summary.t: Jensen Huang stated that Nvidia ‘absolutely must’ work with Chinese AI companies to monitor potential dangers. He emphasized the need for collaborative advancement of the technology to ensure safety, citing ongoing ‘dialogues’ with researchers in China.
Recent discussions around AI safety have intensified, with organizations like OpenAI and Anthropic urging a slowdown in development due to potential existential risks.

articles.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
articles.preview: Reflection's Beam model is now freely available on Ollama for a limited time. The model offers a 1 million token context window and is designed for complex workflows.

articles.title: Mehrere US-Bundesstaaten verklagen KI-Firma OpenAI
articles.preview: Acht US-Bundesstaaten haben OpenAI, den Entwickler von ChatGPT, wegen möglicher Risiken und Schäden durch die KI verklagt. Die Klagen zielen insbesondere auf den Schutz von Kindern und Jugendlichen ab.

summary.h: Die Klagen und die beteiligten Bundesstaaten
summary.t: Acht US-Bundesstaaten, darunter Arizona, Arkansas, Iowa, Nebraska, Kansas, West Virginia, Idaho und Montana, haben OpenAI, den Entwickler von ChatGPT, gemeinsam verklagt. Die Klagen wurden in den jeweiligen Gerichten der Bundesstaaten eingereicht.

Die Bundesstaaten werfen OpenAI vor, nicht ausreichend für den Schutz der Nutzer zu sorgen. Sie argumentieren, ChatGPT sei so konzipiert, dass es Vertrauen erzeugt, aber auch Wahnvorstellungen verstärkt und gefährliches Verhalten fördert.

articles.title: Nvidia, AMD, Dell sink in global tech rout on AI funding worries
articles.preview: AI-related stocks experienced a significant downturn this week, with a total loss of over $1 trillion. This decline was fueled by concerns about financing for massive AI infrastructure projects.

summary.t: A wave of selling pressure impacted global tech stocks, particularly those involved in artificial intelligence and semiconductors. Twenty of the most valuable AI and semiconductor companies lost over $1 trillion in value during the week. Notable declines were seen in Nvidia (-1.84%), AMD (-1.5%), Dell Technologies (-6.8%), SK Hynix (-10%), Samsung Electronics (-8.73%), SoftBank Group (-7.9%), Advantest (-13.95%), Tokyo Electron (-6.45%), Renesas Electronics (-8%), and TSMC (-1.81%).

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s comments helped stabilize the market. He stated that Nvidia did not need to backstop CoreWeave and that the company’s cost of capital was decreasing. This reassured investors and contributed to a recovery in CoreWeave’s stock (+5.94%) and Nebius’ stock (+1.29%).
Investors are worried about the rising cost of financing large-scale AI infrastructure projects.

articles.title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs
articles.preview: Rosalind, an AI model, is now available to academic research labs. This plan provides sponsored access to GPT-Rosalind and related tools.

articles.title: Apple and Meta team up to make Muse AI model run on Mac computers
articles.preview: Apple and Meta are collaborating to enable Meta’s Muse Spark Open AI model to run on Mac computers. This marks a surprising alliance between former rivals, driven by a shared interest in on-device AI capabilities.

summary.h: A Historic Shift in Silicon Valley
summary.t: For years, Apple and Meta operated as competitors, marked by disagreements and limited partnerships. Following John Ternus’s leadership at Apple, and after a period of intense rivalry, the two companies are now collaborating on AI development. This shift comes after Meta’s revenue was impacted by Apple’s privacy changes in 2021, and a long-standing history of animosity between the companies. “Most of the animosity predates my tenure at the company,” stated Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang, highlighting the complex relationship between the two tech giants.

Meta’s Muse Spark Open is an 816-billion-parameter model utilizing a mixture-of-experts architecture. Developers can download the model’s parameters to run locally on hardware, avoiding reliance on the cloud. The model is designed to run efficiently on Apple’s Mac Studio PCs, leveraging the M5 Ultra chip and up to 512GB of memory. Currently, a Mac Studio with the required chip and memory costs at least $10,799, with a higher-end version slated for release later this month offering up to 256GB of RAM.

Running Muse Spark Open locally offers several advantages, including enhanced security and reduced user costs. The collaboration allows developers to utilize Apple’s silicon, specifically the M5 Ultra, and integrate it with Meta’s MLX AI framework. Apple’s technical team has tuned the model for faster performance on Mac hardware, and they are publishing technical documentation to facilitate this process. The move represents a significant step in Apple’s growing interest in AI chips.

Meta has been actively investing in AI development, recently releasing proprietary models like Muse Wonder. The company has purchased hundreds of Mac computers for its Superintelligence team to experiment with local AI and agents.

articles.title: TSMC chip capacity is ‘fierce’ battleground for AI customers, amid record quarter
articles.preview: TSMC is facing intense competition for its chip manufacturing capacity, driven by the booming artificial intelligence industry. The company’s record quarter highlights the unprecedented demand for its advanced semiconductors, creating a bottleneck in the industry’s growth.

summary.t: TSMC is experiencing unprecedented demand for its advanced chips due to the artificial intelligence boom. Jordan Klein of Mizuho Securities describes the competition for factory space as ‘extremely fierce,’ with companies vying for leverage and supply. TSMC can currently only manufacture 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers per year, and customer demand exceeds this capacity.

A growing number of major tech firms, including Apple, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and OpenAI, rely on TSMC to produce custom AI accelerators. TSMC’s CEO, Sajiv Dalal, reports receiving at least 10 calls daily regarding wafer capacity. TSMC anticipates a 58% increase in fourth-quarter revenue compared to the previous year.

Many chipmakers, such as D-Matrix, have cultivated long-term relationships with TSMC, dating back decades. The company’s senior vice president, Kevin Zhang, plays a key role in determining customer access to its factory lines. TSMC is investing heavily in new fabs in Taiwan, Japan, and Arizona, with a total commitment of $265 billion.
TSMC is utilizing tools like ASML’s extreme ultraviolet lithography machines to increase capacity.

articles.title: AWS, Anthropic race to deploy army of specialized engineers key to proving AI spending will pay off
articles.preview: Big Tech companies are investing heavily in a specialized workforce to prove the value of their artificial intelligence investments. These ‘forward deployed engineers’ (FDEs) are crucial for translating AI technology into tangible business results for corporate clients.

summary.t: Several major tech companies are committing significant resources to building a workforce of forward deployed engineers (FDEs). Amazon Web Services (AWS) has pledged $1 billion, OpenAI is investing over $4 billion, and Anthropic is dedicating $100 million to train 10,000 FDEs by 2027. Consulting firms like Accenture and Google Cloud are also building 1,000-person FDE teams. This investment reflects a growing concern among investors that the current AI spending isn't yielding measurable returns.

summary.h: The Role of Forward Deployed Engineers
summary.t: FDEs combine AI and software expertise with a deep understanding of business operations. They work directly with customers to integrate AI systems into existing technology, address security concerns, and overcome organizational obstacles. According to Val Henderson of Caylent, the most critical skill is the ability to understand customer needs and navigate complex business dynamics. The demand for these engineers is rapidly increasing, with job postings surging from under 200 in 2023 to over 7,300 in the first nine months of 2026, accompanied by significantly higher advertised salaries – averaging $195,456.

Companies are employing diverse strategies to develop this specialized talent. AWS is leveraging existing Amazon and AWS engineers, while also recruiting externally. OpenAI is acquiring Tomoro and training engineers from partner organizations through its Claude Frontier Academy, which includes partnerships with firms like Accenture, Bain, and Deloitte. Anthropic’s approach mirrors medical education, pairing experienced engineers with practitioners and assessing them on realistic enterprise deployments. Accenture and Google Cloud are retraining experienced software engineers for customer-facing AI deployment work, with training programs lasting 30 to 90 days.

summary.h: Early Deployment Results and Future Outlook
summary.t: Initial deployments of FDEs have shown improvements in engineering productivity and capacity, such as faster task completion and the freeing up of engineering resources. However, these improvements haven't yet translated into significant financial returns.

articles.title: Teaching students to think and learn through questions
articles.preview: This article announces a new feature, Study Mode, designed to assist teachers. It’s being released in Portuguese and celebrates Teachers’ Day with an AI tool.

articles.title: CoreWeave-Papiere brechen ein: Kreditsorgen ziehen Tech-Werte runter
articles.preview: Die US-Börsen erlitten am Freitag einen weiteren Verkaufsmarathon. Die Sorge um die Finanzierung von KI-Unternehmen, insbesondere CoreWeave, belastet die Technologieaktien stark.

summary.t: Der Nasdaq-Index verlor am Freitag 2,15 Prozent auf 26.140 Punkte. Der S&P 500 brachte 1,1 Prozent auf 7659 Punkte zu Stande und der Dow-Jones sank um 0,34 Prozent auf 52.002 Punkte. Die Technologieaktien waren durch die anhaltenden Bedenken über den KI-Sektor belastet.

Die Papiere von CoreWeave, unterstützt von Nvidia, fielen um zwölf Prozent aufgrund anhaltender Sorgen über die Schuldenlast des Unternehmens. Händler befürchten, dass die hohen Kreditverpflichtungen nicht gedeckt sind.

Auch Micron Technology und Intel verloren jeweils über fünf Prozent. Analysten sehen die Situation als eine Reaktion auf die steigenden Zinsen und die Bedenken hinsichtlich der Rentabilität von KI-Rechenzentren.

articles.title: Tesla's Roadster reveal, Apple and Meta team up, Nike's India push and more in Morning Squawk
articles.preview: This Morning Squawk newsletter covers key market updates, including the Tesla Roadster reveal, a surprising tech partnership, and Nike’s expansion into India. It also addresses concerns about inflation and the Federal Reserve’s future actions.

summary.t: Tesla finally revealed its long-awaited Roadster, showcasing impressive capabilities like hanging upside down and hovering. Production is slated for 2028, with reservations already open for $50,000 among buyers in the U.S., China, and Canada. The vehicle will not include Tesla’s automated driving system.

The producer price index rose significantly, marking the highest monthly and annual increases since 2022. Energy costs, driven by the Iran war, are a key factor, and economists anticipate the core PCE price index will rise later this month, potentially prompting further Federal Reserve action.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh indicated the central bank will not pre-judge future meetings, suggesting the possibility of holding interest rates steady at the next meeting later this month. Traders interpreted this as a lack of immediate plans for further rate hikes.

Apple and Meta announced a collaboration allowing developers to run Meta’s Muse Spark AI model locally on Apple’s Mac computers. This marks a notable shift in alliances within Silicon Valley, driven by the growing AI market.

articles.title: Ausverkauf wegen KI-Sorgen: Techwerte kommen von Tagestiefs zurück
articles.preview: US-Anleger reagieren auf steigende Zinsen und KI-Sorgen. Tech-Aktien fallen deutlich, während andere Sektoren profitieren.

summary.t: Der Dow-Jones Index schloss bei 52.177 Punkten, ein Anstieg von 1,1 Prozent. Der S&P 500 erreichte 7744 Punkte und erhöhte sich um 0,3 Prozent. Der Nasdaq Index blieb mit 26.711 Punkten nahezu unverändert, nachdem er zuvor um rund 400 Punkte gesunken war.
Tech-Aktien gerieten unter Druck aufgrund von Bedenken hinsichtlich hoher Schulden in der KI-Branche. Der Philadelphia Halbleiterindex verzeichnete sieben Handelstage in Folge mit Verlusten.

articles.title: Looking for non-AI stocks to own? Jim Cramer thinks these 2 names are worth buying
articles.preview: Jim Cramer is recommending two apparel stocks, VF Corp and Kontoor Brands, despite concerns about rising interest rates. He believes these companies offer significant buying opportunities due to depressed valuations and shifting fashion trends.

summary.t: Jim Cramer is advising investors to buy VF Corp, the parent company of Vans, The North Face, and Timberland. Recent research indicates a growing interest among teens in non-athletic footwear, particularly Vans. Vans sales have declined nearly 50% since 2022, but the latest teen survey shows stabilization and a rise in popularity among male teens, ranking seventh. Timberland and The North Face have also performed well, entering the top 10 among upper-income teens.

Jim Cramer also recommends Kontoor Brands, formerly a division of VF Corp, which owns Wrangler, Lee, and Helly Hansen. Jefferies upgraded the stock to ‘buy’ and raised the price target to $89, citing a resurgence in denim popularity. Kontoor is expected to benefit from this trend, particularly through Wrangler. The company’s planned $400 million share repurchase program is also a positive factor.

articles.title: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels as investors sour on AI debt
articles.preview: CoreWeave's credit default swap rates have dramatically increased, signaling investor concerns about the company's substantial AI-related debt. This rise in risk is impacting other neocloud stocks and broader AI investments.

summary.t: CoreWeave has accumulated over $51 billion in debt to finance its AI infrastructure. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 reached 15.78% as investors expressed concern about the company’s financial situation.

The spread on CoreWeave’s five-year credit default swaps rose dramatically, peaking at 1,140 basis points. This represents a 16% week-over-week increase and a 164% jump compared to a year ago, indicating heightened investor risk perception.

The concerns surrounding CoreWeave’s debt have spread to other neocloud stocks, with Nebius and Iren also experiencing declines. Additionally, shares of Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices fell following the broader sell-off in South Korean chip stocks.

articles.title: Viele Kurse fallen immer weiter: Ausverkauf von Tech-Aktien an US-Börsen vernichtet Billionenwerte
articles.preview: Die US-Börsen erleben einen massiven Ausverkauf von Technologieaktien. Die Stimmung ist insgesamt durch Unsicherheiten und hohe Zinsen getrübt.

summary.t: Der Dow-Jones Index notierte am Morgen 0,3 Prozent höher bei 51.755 Punkten. Der S&P 500 verlor 0,6 Prozent auf 7672 Zähler. Der Nasdaq Index fiel um 1,4 Prozent auf 26.309 Punkte.
Der Philadelphia Halbleiter-Index verzeichnete Verluste von über zwei Billionen Dollar an Börsenwert nach sieben Verlusttagen. TSMC gab eine vorsichtige Prognose für 2027 ab.

articles.title: Furcht vor einer Insolvenzwelle: Tech-Ausverkauf erfasst Europas Börsen
articles.preview: Die europäischen Aktienmärkte erleben einen erheblichen Ausverkauf im Technologiesektor. Dies wird durch steigende Zinsen, hohe Bewertungen und Zweifel an der Rentabilität von KI-Investitionen verstärkt.

summary.t: Der DAX verzeichnete um rund ein Prozent an Wert und notierte bei 25.173 Punkten. Der EuroStoxx50 fiel um rund ein Prozent auf 6133 Zähler. Besonders stark betroffen war der europäische Technologie-Branchenindex, der um drei Prozent an Wert verlor. Die Aktien von Infineon, Aixtron und Suss Microtec brachen um acht bis neun Prozent ein.

Die Sorgen um den Technologiesektor breiteten sich global aus. In Japan und Südkorea fielen die Technologieindizes um rund 5 und 7,5 Prozent, während der Nasdaq in den USA um knapp zwei Prozent abwertete. Analysten sehen dies nicht als klassische Gewinnmitnahme, sondern als Warnsignal vor einer Korrektur.

articles.title: Marktbericht: TSMC gibt sich keine Blöße
articles.preview: TSMC hat einen neuen Rekordgewinn erzielt. Die Nachfrage nach Chips, insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit dem KI-Boom, ist weiterhin extrem hoch.

summary.t: Der taiwanesische Chip-Auftragsfertiger TSMC hat einen Umsatz von 41,66 Milliarden Euro erzielt, was einen Anstieg von 50 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahr darstellt. Das Unternehmen prognostiziert ein Wachstum von 55 bis 61 Prozent für das laufende Quartal und erwartet einen Gesamtjahresumsatzsteigerung von 44 Prozent.

Aufgrund der enormen Nachfrage nach Chips, getrieben durch den KI-Boom, arbeitet TSMC intensiv an der Ausweitung seiner Produktionskapazitäten. Das Unternehmen bestätigte sein Investitionsziel von 64 Milliarden Dollar, um die Anleger zu beruhigen.

Trotz der beeindruckenden Ergebnisse von TSMC und der Rekordquartale des Unternehmens, bleiben die Anleger vorsichtig. Die Sorge vor steigenden Zinsen und die Finanzierungsabhängigkeit von Tech-Unternehmen, insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit dem Bau von Rechenzentren, führen zu Unsicherheit.

Die Börsenverluste sind global ausgeprägt. Der Nasdaq-Index in den USA verzeichnete am Vortag einen deutlichen Rückgang, während auch der Kospi in Südkorea um rund neun Prozent und der Nikkei-Index in Japan um fast fünf Prozent sanken.

articles.title: Memory stocks are getting hammered. China and a 2029 oversupply are the big worries
articles.preview: Memory chip stocks are experiencing a significant downturn. Concerns about Chinese competition and potential oversupply are driving the market's instability.

summary.t: Shares of SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron have fallen sharply. This decline is fueled by the announcement of a new server memory product from ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) in China. CXMT's innovative design raises fears of increased market share for the Chinese company.

Analysts question CXMT’s ability to scale production. Concerns center around the potential for low production yields, where a significant portion of chips fail to function correctly. Ben Barringer highlighted the importance of yield rates in chip manufacturing.

Senior research analyst Kevin Cassidy believes CXMT’s developments won’t significantly impact supply. Furthermore, a report in Maeil Business Newspaper warns of a potential memory market flood in 2029, driven by an anticipated boom in AI, with Elon Musk adding to the concern about increased Chinese RAM production in 2028.
